threads.thread_goal: Align on scope, sectors, and case types for the standardisation project.

messages.text:
Kicking off the Cross-Sector Digital Intake and Case-Handling Standardisation work.

Goal for this thread: agree which case types per sector we include in the first wave and confirm the 30-day timeline and milestones.

From the backlog, T1–T4 will give us the current-state view, and A1 will hold the process maps once we draft them.

Initial proposal for scope:
- Health: outpatient referrals and follow-up appointments
- Education: special support needs assessments
- Courts: standard civil claims (no criminal)
- Civil service: general citizen enquiries (non-urgent)

Tentative milestones within 30 days:
Week 1: complete T1–T4 and upload to A1
Week 2: align on unified data model and draft forms
Week 3: confidentiality guideline and SOP draft
Week 4: pilot prep and sign-offs

Can you all react to the case types and timeline so we can lock them in?

From the medical side, outpatient referrals and follow-up appointments are fine for a first wave.

One nuance: intake for urgent referrals can be a bit different from routine ones. For T1, I can map both but we might want to limit the standardisation pilot to routine outpatient referrals only, otherwise we risk mixing emergency flows.

On the timeline, I will need a couple of days to collect all current forms and templates for T1 before we can finalise A1 for health. Week 1 is doable if I start today.

On the court side, standard civil claims are a good starting point.

For T3, I suggest we narrow it further to uncontested civil claims and small claims. Those have clearer intake rules and fewer exceptions, and they are easier to map in A1.

Week 1 for T3 is realistic if I can get a second officer to validate the process map as required. I will coordinate that internally.

For civil service, general citizen enquiries is a broad category.

To keep T4 manageable, I propose we focus on written enquiries (email and web forms) about benefits and registrations, excluding complaints and appeals for this first wave. Those have clearer routing rules and will be easier to standardise.

Timeline-wise, your week-by-week outline looks workable. We should probably add explicit check-ins:
- End of week 1: review A1 draft together
- Mid week 2: confirm data model and minimum data set
- End of week 3: sign off on confidentiality guideline and SOP drafts for pilot

If we agree, we can record this as our baseline plan.

Adding to what 60035 said: for courts, if we include small claims, we should be clear whether we cover both paper and digital filings in T3.

For the pilot, I would suggest we only standardise the digital intake side first, and keep paper as-is, otherwise we might overload frontline staff.

The 30-day window is tight but acceptable if we keep the scope narrow like this.

Thanks all, summarising the scope proposals so far:
- Health: routine outpatient referrals and follow-up appointments (exclude emergency flows for now)
- Education: I had suggested special support needs assessments, but I can still adjust that if needed
- Courts: uncontested civil claims and small claims, digital intake only for the pilot
- Civil service: written enquiries (email and web) about benefits and registrations, excluding complaints and appeals

If there are no objections, we can treat this as the first-wave scope and move on to locking the timeline.

From my side, that scope works.

On education, special support needs assessments are a good fit because they already involve multiple stakeholders and clear documentation. They will give us a solid test case for cross-sector alignment later.

On the timeline, I support your week-by-week structure. We just need to be disciplined about the review points so that T1–T4 feed into the later tasks without delay.

No objections from health.

For T1, I will focus on routine outpatient referrals and follow-ups as discussed. I will still note where emergency intake diverges, but we can clearly mark that as out of scope for this wave in A1.

The week 1 deadline is fine as long as we keep the mapping at a practical level, not every rare exception.

Courts are aligned with that scope.

For T3, I will map uncontested civil claims and small claims, digital intake only, and I will flag where paper intake differs so we can consider it in a later wave.

The 30-day structure is acceptable. The only risk I see is if legal review of any draft takes longer than expected, but we can escalate that to our managers if needed.

Agree with the court scope and the 30-day outline.

I can support 60035 with validation on T3 so we meet the week 1 target for A1.

Great, sounds like we have convergence.

To make it explicit:
- First-wave case types per sector are as summarised above
- Overall timeline is 30 days with these key milestones:
  - End of week 1: T1–T4 completed and captured in A1
  - Mid week 2: unified data model and minimum data set drafted (T5) and shared
  - End of week 2: sector form drafts started (T6, T7)
  - End of week 3: confidentiality guideline (T8) and SOP draft (T9)
  - Week 4: checklists (T10), pilot planning (T11) and feedback plan (T12)

Unless anyone disagrees today, I will record this as our agreed scope and timeline.

No disagreement from me.

I suggest we also note that the pilot will be limited to a small number of case types per sector, as you described, to stay within the 30-day window and avoid changes to core systems.

From my side, we can treat this as confirmed.
Confirmed for courts as well. The milestones and scope are clear enough for us to start T3 immediately.

Confirmed from health.

I will start gathering the current forms and mapping the steps for T1 this afternoon so we can hit the week 1 milestone for A1.

Thanks all, recording that we have:
- Agreed first-wave case types per sector
- Confirmed the 30-day timeline and key milestones

I will draft a short summary note and store it alongside A1 so we can reference it during the rest of the project.

threads.thread_goal: Review and finalise the unified intake data model and standard forms.

messages.text:
I have put together a first draft of the unified intake data model and minimum data set based on the current-state maps in A1 and the scope we agreed.

The draft is in A2 and linked to T5. Structure:
- Section 1: common fields across all sectors (person identification, contact details, consent, channel, date/time)
- Section 2: sector-specific mandatory fields (health, education, courts, civil service)
- Section 3: optional fields that we might phase in later

For health and courts, this should feed directly into T6 and T7 when you design your sector forms.

Can you review A2 and comment on any missing or unnecessary fields before we freeze the minimum data set?

I have gone through A2.

Overall structure looks good. A few comments:
- Common fields: we should add a field for preferred communication channel and language, as this affects how we handle follow-up across sectors.
- Civil service section: for benefits enquiries, we need a field for type of benefit and a short free-text description of the request.

These additions should not complicate T6 or T7 but will help with routing and reporting.

Once we agree on these tweaks, I am comfortable treating the common section as stable for the pilot.

I reviewed the health part of A2.

For medical intake, we should include:
- Referring provider details (name, organisation, contact)
- Clinical priority (routine vs urgent) even if we only pilot routine cases, so staff can still flag urgency
- Consent for sharing information with other providers

If we add these to the health-specific section, I can align T6 with A2 without extra custom fields.

No objections to the common fields from my side.

Looking at the court section in A2.

We need to ensure we capture:
- Case type (uncontested civil, small claim)
- Court location
- Statutory deadline or limitation date
- List of attached evidence items

Some of these are already in your draft, but I do not see a clear field for statutory deadline. That is critical for T7 so we can structure the form around time limits.

If we add that, I think the court-specific fields will be sufficient for the pilot.

Agree with 60035. We also often need a field for representation (self-represented or represented by a lawyer) in court cases.

Could we add that to the court section in A2? It will help us design T7 so that we ask for the right contact details.

Thanks for the detailed comments.

I will update A2 with:
- Preferred communication channel and language in the common section
- Benefit type and short description in the civil service section
- Referring provider, clinical priority, and consent for information sharing in the health section
- Statutory deadline and representation status in the court section

Once I push these changes, can each of you confirm that the updated A2 covers your minimum needs for the pilot so we can close T5?

I have rechecked the updated A2.

The new common and civil service fields look good and still keep the model lean.

From civil service, I am fine treating this as the agreed minimum data set for the pilot.

I confirm that the health section in A2 now has the fields we need.

For T6, I will mirror the structure of A2 so that we do not introduce extra variations.

From health, the unified data model is acceptable for the pilot.

I checked the court section again.

Statutory deadline and representation status are now clearly included in A2.

This is sufficient for us to proceed with T7. I am comfortable treating the court part of the data model as final for the pilot.

Confirming from my side as well: the court fields in A2 cover what we need for the pilot forms.

No further changes requested.

Thanks everyone.

Based on your confirmations, I will mark T5 as complete and treat A2 as the approved unified intake data model and minimum data set for the pilot.

Next step is to finalise the sector forms:
- T6: health digital intake form
- T7: court digital intake form

Please share when your drafts are ready so we can sign them off for pilot use.

I have created a first draft of the health digital intake form for T6, using the fields from A2.

Format: standard office document with sections for patient details, referral details, clinical priority, and consent.

I tested it with two sample outpatient referrals and it worked, but I would appreciate a quick look from the rest of you to see if anything is unclear before we sign off.

For T7, I have drafted the court digital intake form based on A2.

It includes sections for party details, representation, case type, court location, statutory deadline, and evidence list.

I have checked it against our standard procedures and the civil process order. I will ask another court officer to review it today so we meet the requirement for a second approval.

I have reviewed the T7 draft.

The structure is clear and matches the fields in A2. I tested it with a small claim example and it captured all the necessary information.

From my side, I approve this version for pilot use.

I checked the health form draft for T6.

It aligns with A2 and the sections are easy to follow. The consent wording looks consistent with what we will include in the cross-sector guideline later.

I suggest we accept this version for the pilot and adjust only if the pilot feedback shows issues.

Summarising where we are:
- A2 is approved as the unified intake data model and minimum data set for the pilot
- T6: health digital intake form drafted, tested with sample cases, and reviewed
- T7: court digital intake form drafted, checked against procedures, and approved by a second officer

Unless there are last-minute objections, we can sign off both sector forms for pilot use.

threads.thread_goal: Agree on confidentiality rules and how they apply in the new workflow.

messages.text:
I have drafted the cross-sector confidentiality and data handling guideline for T8.

The draft is stored as A3 and structured as follows:
- Section 1: shared principles across health, education, courts, and civil service
- Section 2: access control rules (who can see what, in which situations)
- Section 3: document sharing and storage practices
- Section 4: incident reporting and escalation

This is based on the sector rules you shared while working on A1 and T1–T4.

Please review A3 and comment on anything that conflicts with your sector rules or is unclear for frontline staff.

I have reviewed A3 from the court perspective.

Overall, the shared principles and access control rules are compatible with our obligations, but I have two comments:
- For court case files, access should be restricted to staff assigned to the case and their direct supervisors, except where law provides for public access.
- Evidence handling: we should explicitly state that sensitive evidence (e.g. medical reports) must not be shared by email unless encrypted or via approved channels.

If we add these clarifications, I believe A3 will be acceptable for courts.

From the medical side, A3 looks mostly aligned with our current practice.

I would suggest we emphasise:
- Minimum necessary information: staff should only access and share the data needed for the specific task.
- Use of shared drives: medical documents should be stored only in approved systems, not on local devices.

These points are already implied, but making them explicit will help when we train staff later.

I checked A3 with an eye on how it will link into the SOP in T9.

The structure works well. For education, we should add a note that access to student records is limited to staff with a legitimate educational interest, and that sharing with external parties requires documented consent or a clear legal basis.

If we include that, I can reference A3 directly in the relevant steps of the unified workflow.

I also went through A3.

The only thing I would add is a simple checklist-style summary at the end for frontline staff: do not print unless necessary, do not leave files unattended, lock your screen, and so on.

That might overlap with A5 later, but having it in A3 will help reinforce the message.

Thanks for the feedback.

I will update A3 to include:
- Court-specific access restrictions for case files and supervisors
- Explicit rule on handling sensitive evidence and avoiding unencrypted email
- Medical minimum-necessary principle and storage in approved systems only
- Education rule on legitimate interest and external sharing
- A short checklist at the end for everyday behaviour

Once the updated version is in place, could each of you confirm that it does not conflict with your sector rules?

I have rechecked the updated A3.

The new court-specific wording is consistent with our procedures and the civil process order.

From courts, I am comfortable adopting this guideline for the pilot.

I confirm that the medical additions in A3 look good.

They match what our data protection officer usually emphasises, so I do not see any conflicts.

Education part in A3 is now clear.

I will make sure the SOP steps in T9 reference the relevant sections so staff know when to check the guideline.

The checklist at the end of A3 is very helpful.

No further comments from my side.

Thanks all for reviewing.

Given your confirmations and the fact that A3 now reflects the key sector rules, I propose we approve this version as the cross-sector confidentiality and data handling guideline for the pilot.

I will also ensure it is version-controlled and shared with all stakeholders as required in T8.

threads.thread_goal: Validate the unified intake workflow, SOP, and frontline checklists.

messages.text:
I have drafted the unified intake workflow and SOP for T9, and a first set of frontline checklists for T10.

Documents:
- A4: Unified Intake Workflow and SOP
- A5: Frontline Intake Quick-Reference Checklists (one per sector)

The SOP references A2 for data fields and A3 for confidentiality rules.

Could each of you take one or two sample cases in your sector and walk through A4 using the relevant checklist from A5, then share any issues or missing steps?

I tested A4 and the health checklist in A5 with two routine outpatient referrals.

Observations:
- The steps are generally clear, but the SOP could mention explicitly when to check existing patient records before creating a new one.
- The checklist is helpful, though it might be useful to add a reminder to verify consent is recorded before sharing documents with external providers.

If we add those two points, I think health staff will be able to follow the workflow without confusion.

I ran through A4 and the court checklist in A5 using a small claim example.

Findings:
- The intake steps match our practice, but we should highlight the point where statutory deadlines from A2 must be checked and recorded.
- The checklist could include a line to confirm that all mandatory evidence items are attached before registering the case.

With these adjustments, the workflow should work well for courts in the pilot.

I also tried A4 and the court checklist with an uncontested civil claim.

The only extra suggestion I have is to add a reminder in the checklist to verify representation status and capture the correct contact details.

Otherwise, the flow felt natural.

I tested A4 and the civil service checklist in A5 with two written enquiries about benefits.

Comments:
- The routing step could be clearer about when to escalate to a specialist unit versus handling at first line.
- The checklist should include a quick check that the enquiry type and benefit type fields from A2 are filled in, to support reporting later.

These are small edits, but they will help frontline staff make consistent decisions.

Thanks for the tests and comments.

I will update A4 to:
- Add a step in the health flow to check existing records before creating new ones
- Emphasise the statutory deadline check in the court flow
- Clarify escalation rules for civil service enquiries

And I will update A5 to:
- Add consent verification for health
- Add evidence completeness and representation status checks for courts
- Add enquiry type and benefit type checks for civil service

Once updated, I will let you know so you can do a quick final read.

I have rechecked the health parts of A4 and the health checklist in A5.

The new steps and reminders cover the gaps I mentioned. I do not see any remaining issues for the pilot.

Court sections in A4 and the court checklist in A5 now clearly call out the statutory deadline and evidence checks.

From courts, I am fine using these in the pilot.

Confirming that the representation reminder is now in the court checklist in A5.

No further comments.

The civil service flow and checklist updates look good.

The escalation criteria and field checks are now explicit, which should reduce inconsistent handling.

Thanks for validating the changes.

To summarise:
- A4 now reflects the agreed intake steps for all sectors and references A2 and A3 where needed
- A5 contains updated checklists per sector with the key checks you highlighted

If everyone agrees, we can approve A4 as the workflow and SOP for pilot implementation and A5 as the final set of frontline checklists.

threads.thread_goal: Plan the pilot, track issues, and agree on improvement actions.

messages.text:
With A4 and A5 ready, we should align on the pilot plan and tracking.

For T11, I propose the following pilot scope and schedule:
- Duration: 2 weeks
- Health: first 20 routine outpatient referrals using the new form and checklist
- Education: first 15 special support needs assessments
- Courts: first 20 uncontested civil or small claims filed digitally
- Civil service: first 30 written enquiries about benefits and registrations

Tracking:
- A6 as the shared pilot tracking and feedback log
- Each sector logs cases daily with basic metrics (processing time, errors, rework, issues)

Success criteria (initial draft):
- No increase in critical errors compared to current process
- At least 10 percent reduction in average intake processing time for pilot cases
- Staff feedback not indicating major usability problems

Please react to the scope, tracking approach, and criteria so we can finalise T11.

For health, 20 routine outpatient referrals over 2 weeks is manageable.

On tracking in A6, I suggest we add a simple field for whether the case required clarification from the referrer. That will help us see if the new form reduces back-and-forth.

The success criteria look reasonable, though measuring the 10 percent time reduction might require a quick baseline estimate from our current process.

Courts can commit to 20 digital uncontested or small claims for the pilot.

For A6, we should also capture whether statutory deadlines were correctly recorded at intake. That is a key risk area for us.

On success criteria, I agree with the error and time targets, but we should also track whether any pilot case leads to a complaint related to intake handling.

Agree with 60035 on tracking complaints.

Maybe we can add a simple yes or no field in A6 for whether the case triggered a complaint or formal query about intake.

For education, 15 special support needs assessments is fine.

On success criteria, I would add a qualitative element: at least neutral or better feedback from staff on clarity of A4 and A5, collected via a short survey at the end of the pilot.

I can help design a simple survey and link the results into T12 and A7.

Good suggestions.

I will update A6 to include fields for:
- Clarification needed from referrer (yes or no)
- Statutory deadline correctly recorded (yes or no, for courts)
- Complaint or formal query triggered (yes or no)

For the time reduction, we can ask each sector to provide a rough baseline for current average intake time before the pilot starts, and then compare with the pilot data.

Health is fine with that.

I can provide a rough baseline for current intake time based on a small sample from last week and log the pilot cases daily in A6.

Courts agree with the updated tracking fields in A6.

We will also monitor if any pilot case leads to a complaint and record it there.
Confirmed from my side as well. The tracking structure in A6 looks practical enough for daily logging.

I will prepare a short staff survey for the end of the pilot and link the results into T12 and A7.

For the pilot scope and success criteria, I am comfortable with what 388919 proposed, plus the additions we discussed.

Great, summarising the pilot plan for T11:
- Scope: 2-week pilot with the case volumes per sector as proposed
- Tracking: A6 with fields for processing time, errors, rework, clarifications, statutory deadline correctness, and complaints
- Success criteria:
  - No increase in critical errors
  - Around 10 percent reduction in average intake time compared to baseline
  - No significant increase in complaints related to intake
  - Staff feedback at least neutral on clarity and usability of A4 and A5

If there are no objections, I will treat this as our agreed pilot scope, tracking approach, and success criteria.

Courts agree with this pilot plan and criteria.

We are ready to start logging cases in A6 once the pilot begins.

Health is aligned as well.

No further changes from my side.

Education agrees with the scope, tracking, and success criteria.

I will make sure we log our pilot cases daily and collect staff feedback for T12.

Thanks everyone.

We will proceed with this pilot setup and use A6 as the central log.

After the pilot, we will consolidate feedback and metrics under T12 and produce the final report in A7.
